github.title: Make launcher stop end the session by /exit on Herdr and with background tasks
github.author: jerridan

identity.head: 7e19451a9f97486355cf48360d0a0bfe17001f5f
identity.description:
Make launcher stop end the session by /exit on Herdr and with background tasks

## Summary

The launcher's `stop` command must end an implementer's Claude Code session with `/exit` before it closes the tab. In two cases it closed the tab over a live session. On the Herdr terminal, `/exit` reached the session as a message to the model and not as a command. On each terminal, a session with a live background task answers `/exit` with a confirmation dialog and does not end. Now `stop` types `/exit` as keys on Herdr, and on each terminal it reads the screen and presses Enter one time when the screen shows that dialog. Only the seeded test ran the change: no live session got these keys.

**Ticket:** N/A
**Type:** Bug fix

---

## Agent context

### Authority

- `docs/design.md` §15.155 (new) records the two causes, the decisions and the parts that no live run has shown. §15.153 is the Herdr terminal of the launcher.
- `skills/orchestrator/references/launcher.md`, section `focus and stop`, owns what `stop` sends and the screen check.

### What changed, by file

- `skills/orchestrator/scripts/launcher.py`: on Herdr, `stop` runs `hc keys <t> / e x i t` and then `hc keys <t> enter`, and no longer runs `hc send <t> /exit --force`. `wait_claude_gone` takes a `confirm` step. While a `claude` process stays on the tty, each poll reads the screen (`tmux capture-pane -p -t <pane>`, `hc read <t>`, or `contents` of the iTerm2 session through the new `OSA_SCREEN`). When `shows_exit_dialog` is true, `stop` presses Enter one time (`tmux send-keys Enter`, `hc keys <t> enter`, or `write text ""` through the new `OSA_ENTER`) and the 15 seconds start again. A screen read or a key that fails in this step sends nothing more and is no failure of `stop`.
- `skills/orchestrator/scripts/test-launcher.sh`: the `tmux`, `osascript` and `hc` stubs answer a screen read from a file, and `confirm-ends` makes the second Enter end the stub `claude`. Eight new checks cover the exit dialog on the three terminals, a permission dialog under the words of the exit dialog, a screen with no dialog, and a stop with no `claude` left. The Herdr stop checks now expect `hc keys` and no `hc send`. The stub files `hc-send-fail` and `hc-send-gone` are now `hc-exit-fail` and `hc-exit-gone`.
- `skills/orchestrator/references/launcher.md`: the keys of Herdr, the exit dialog step and its screen check, and a `Limit: the keys` list of each part that no live run has shown.
- `docs/design.md`: §15.155.
- `.claude-plugin/plugin.json`, `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json`: version 0.1.123.

### Constraints that applied

- `stop` sends nothing that can approve a permission dialog. The only new key is Enter, and `stop` sends it only when the screen ends with the exit dialog: a title line, then `Exit and stop tasks`, then `Stay`, then at most 6 lines with text, none of which starts a numbered option. A permission dialog has numbered options. Escape still comes first.
- `stop` sends nothing that reaches the model as a prompt. On Herdr it no longer runs `hc send`, which put `/exit` in an `<hc>` tag. Ctrl-U still clears the input line before `/exit`.
- A session with no background task gets the same keys as before on tmux and iTerm2. `stop` reads no screen when no `claude` is on the tty at the first poll.
- A change to what the plugin loads sets the version in both manifests: 0.1.123 in each.
- A rule lives in one file: `launcher.md` owns the keys and the check, and §15.155 points at it.
- The limits of the work: no `claude` process started, and no key or message went to a live tab, pane or Herdr terminal.

### How this was verified

- `bash skills/orchestrator/scripts/test-launcher.sh` printed `288 of 288 checks passed`. Before the code change, the same test with the new checks printed `277 of 288 checks passed`: the 11 red checks were the 7 new checks that need the change and the 4 Herdr checks that expect `hc keys`.
- The dialog texts, the focus on the first option and the exit reason come from a read of the Claude Code binaries 2.1.326, 2.1.330 and 2.1.331: `requestExit`, the component with `tengu_exit_background_work_prompt`, and the function that ends with `prompt_input_exit`.
- `hc keys --help`, `hc send --help` and `hc read --help` gave the command shapes. `hc read` prints the screen only, with `--lines 0` as its default.

### Known gaps

- No live run has shown that `hc keys` takes `/` as a key name, or that a Herdr session runs the typed `/exit` as a command. If `hc` refuses the key, `stop` exits 6 and the tab stays open.
- Nobody saw the exit dialog on a screen. The screen check is a guess at its layout. If it does not match, `stop` sends no Enter and closes the tab over the live session, as before this change.
- No live run has shown the screen read on any terminal, the `contents` property of an iTerm2 session, or Enter on the dialog.
- `stop` does not answer the other exit dialog of that code, for a session whose worktree Claude Code made.
- Escape, Ctrl-U and `/exit` on iTerm2 stay without a live run.

findings.claim: When the session already shows the exit dialog before stop runs (for example, someone typed /exit by hand), stop's Escape cancels that dialog and /exit opens it again. Because the first screen read matched, exit_confirm returns None, so stop never presses Enter and closes the tab over the live session.
findings.suggested_fix: Read the screen again after Escape and Ctrl-U, before /exit. Use that read to decide whether the dialog was already there.
findings.explanation: The guard against an existing dialog skips the case that most likely caused it: a pending exit dialog from an earlier /exit, which the Escape step dismisses and /exit then shows again.

findings.claim: wait_claude_gone calls confirm on every poll, and each call runs a screen read: hc read with a 60 s timeout, or osascript with no timeout. One slow read can push the stop far past STOP_WAIT.
findings.evidence: rc, out, err = run([hc, "read", ref], timeout=60)
findings.suggested_fix: Give the screen reads a short timeout (a few seconds), or limit each read to the time left in the wait.
findings.explanation: The deadline in wait_claude_gone is only checked between polls, so it does not limit a screen read that blocks inside confirm.

findings.claim: On iTerm2, OSA_ENTER returns "gone" without an error when it cannot find the session. confirm still treats this as a pressed Enter: it returns True, the wait restarts and no later poll tries again.
findings.evidence: confirm = exit_confirm(lambda: iterm_screen(ref), lambda: iterm_script(OSA_ENTER, "enter", ref))
findings.suggested_fix: Raise Fail when the enter script returns "gone", so confirm returns False.
findings.explanation: A "gone" result means no Enter was pressed, but the code counts it as a successful confirm.

findings.claim: The screen check decides whether to press Enter from text that the session itself can print, so printed text shaped like the exit dialog above a prompt with no numbered options can lead `stop` to press Enter on another prompt.
findings.evidence: return len(tail) <= EXIT_DIALOG_TAIL and not any(OPTION_RE.match(l) for l in tail)
findings.suggested_fix: Also check that the focus pointer is on the 'Exit and stop tasks' line, or that a frame or style that only Claude Code's own UI draws is present, before pressing Enter.
findings.explanation: Text on the screen that the model or a tool controls can make the check true, and the Enter that follows could confirm a prompt that has no numbered options.

findings.claim: The confirm-step test relies on real wall-clock timing windows (3.0–4.5 s) and 1.2 s thresholds, and bundles several behaviours in one check.
findings.evidence: if not 3.0 <= took < 4.5: bad.append("the wait starts again at the confirm: %.1f" % took)
findings.suggested_fix: Patch launcher.time (time.time and sleep) with a fake clock, and split the behaviours into separate checks.
findings.explanation: Real sleeps with tight bounds can flake on a loaded machine, and one pass/fail check covers many behaviours, so a failure does not say which broke. A fake clock would be deterministic.

below_floor.span_text: """A confirm step for wait_claude_gone, or None. Call it before the first key of stop: it reads the screen one time now.
